items.title: Vultrino – Let AI agents use credentials without seeing them
items.raw_excerpt:
I built Vultrino because I kept running into the same problem: I want AI agents to do things
that require credentials, but I don't want those secrets in prompts, logs, or context windows. It's not just API keys – it's signing commits with PGP keys, accessing databases, decrypting
files, anything that needs a secret. The agent shouldn't see the credential; it should just be
able to use it. Vultrino is a credential proxy that sits between your AI agent and the operation. The agent says "use my github-api credential" or "sign this with my pgp-key" and Vultrino handles the secret
material without exposing it. Key features:
- WASM plugin system – add any credential type (PGP signing plugin included, build your own)
- MCP native – works directly with Claude
- OAuth2 with automatic token refresh

Most monitoring tools are expensive SaaS products that charge per check. Test automation and monitoring are often separate concerns, using different tools and workflows. We wanted a unified platform where you can write a Playwright test once and use it for both CI/CD testing and production monitoring and use same tool for k6 performance tests too. *What Supercheck Does:* Testing:
- Playwright browser tests (UI/E2E) with screenshots, traces, videos
- API tests (HTTP/GraphQL)
- Database tests (PostgreSQL, MySQL)
- k6 performance tests
- Schedule tests via cron or trigger from CI/CD Monitoring:
- HTTP, Website, Ping, Port monitors
- Synthetic mon

Physical AI, which refers to intelligent agents that interact with the real world, is becoming one of the most talked-about topics in the tech community. The appearance of various forms of robots at CES 2026 is testing the boundaries and possibilities of Physical AI. During CES 2026, Professor Amnon Shashua, founder, president, and CEO of Mobileye, stated in an interview with Leiphone: "Cars and robots are currently the two most typical application scenarios for Physical AI." Mobileye is not a bystander in either of these directions.  
Automotive is Mobileye's long-established and well-known foundation, while robotics represents its newly showcased growth engine. As artificial intelligence transitions from conversation to real-life applications, human society stands at a new crossroads. On January 27, 2026, the Tencent Tech for Good Innovation Festival (2026), hosted by the Tencent Research Institute, was held in Shenzhen. Under the theme "Happening Now," this year's festival brought together 53 experts, scholars, industry leaders, and practitioners from fields such as global technology, humanities, arts, and education to explore the profound changes occurring in individual lives, industrial structures, and social frameworks amid the rapid evolution of AI.

In the opening address, Guo Kaitian, Senior Vice President of Tencent Group and Chairman of the Tencent Research Institute, stated that artificial intelligence represents a profound transformation on a century-long scale, which must be approached with the patience of long-termism, advanced with confidence in universal empowerment, and guided by a socially benevolent intent. He emphasized that AI is not a tool for short-term competition but a marathon requiring sustained investment and co-creation with users and society. Its value lies not in replacing humans but in amplifying human capabilities and helping more ordinary people gain skills and opportunities. Guo Kaitian also stressed that tech companies must pay close attention to groups with weaker adaptability and limited resources during the accelerated development of AI, avoiding the widening of structural disparities by technological dividends. In his view, although the path of AI development is fraught with uncertainty, one consensus should be clear: AI must be guided by a clear and steadfast "tech for good" value system, ensuring its development remains accountable to people and society.
